trĭentābŭlum , i, n. triens,
I.a portion of public land assigned to creditors in place of a third part of the public debt: “trientabulumque is ager, quia pro tertiā parte pecuniae datus erat, appellatus,” Liv. 31, 13, 9 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
